# matchedfilter COST table -- RELATIVE cost per configuration, measured
#
# cpu     AMD RYZEN AI MAX+ 395 w/ Radeon 8060S
# commit  14e598a
# trials  48 references x 32 configurations, 3 timed passes each
#
# The number is cost RELATIVE to the pivot configuration band 1024, U 2, K 8,
# margin 1.00 -- not microseconds.  Absolute time is a property of machine, load
# and reference together; the ratio is a property of the configuration, which
# is the only thing selection needs, since it never compares across machines
# or across references.
#
# Measured by holding ONE reference fixed and timing every configuration on
# it, cycling the configurations rather than running each to completion, and
# dividing by a pivot measured in the same loop.  Clock and turbo state,
# contention, cache temperature and the machine itself are common to all
# configurations in a pass and cancel in the ratio.  Residual spread across
# passes was 2.1% median, 18.5% worst.
#
# The f and beff on a row are the reference's OWN in-band fraction and
# effective bandwidth AT THAT BAND -- what the library recomputes at selection
# time.  An earlier table built a separate reference per cell from nominal
# (f, beff), so band 512 and band 1024 were timed on different signals and
# ranked against each other.  That is not a noisy comparison, it is not a
# comparison, and it made selection pick the slowest of four admissible
# options (20.30 ms/segment where 13.29 was available).
#
# Must be measured on NOISE: the coarse threshold sets the trigger rate, which is the
# coarse-to-reconstruction ratio and therefore most of the cost.
#
# Regenerate locally for your own CPU:
#   python tools/hmf_tune.py --retune-cost --out mycost.txt
#   export MF_COST=$PWD/mycost.txt
#
# COST n band U K snr f beff coarse_margin relative_cost
